title: Bike — one Math Engine, tubes and rings
description:
A parametric BICYCLE on the same six-node spine as table_with_math.json — Geometry → Input Properties → Math Engine → Output Metrics → 2D Render + 3D Render — and the flow the Stroke / Tube / Ring render rows were added for.

SELECT A NODE, A SEGMENT OR A SPACE on canvas, or leave nothing selected and the bike is built at the flow anchor.

WHAT A BIKE IS, GEOMETRICALLY. Not a stack of boxes: it is 27 SEGMENTS and 4 CIRCLES OF REVOLUTION, almost none of them axis-aligned. A diamond frame's down tube, its paired chain and seat stays, a raked fork, a crank arm, a wheel standing on edge — every one of them is a solid ABOUT AN ARBITRARY AXIS, which is exactly what the render nodes could not express before this flow. A Cuboid or Cylinder row is positioned by a POINT and its axis is fixed vertical; the row carries no rotation and no wire can reach one. The only way through was to hand-author faces into a Polyhedron row, i.e. to write a mesher in the Math Engine — which is how the prism in inset_with_math.json is built, and it costs six lines for ONE extrusion.

SO THREE ROW KINDS WERE ADDED, and they share one wire format:
• 3D TUBE — a capped cylinder along a wired AXIS SEGMENT `[[x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2],…]`, one per row of the list, radius from the row or from a SEVENTH column per segment.
• 3D RING — a torus whose AXIS is that same segment: centred on its MIDPOINT, lying in the perpendicular plane. Only direction and midpoint are read — the LENGTH is free — so a wheel is driven by its axle, which is the honest description of a wheel. Radius is the ring, Tube radius the section; a seventh column overrides the first and an eighth the second.
• 2D STROKE — the plan twin: a SEGMENT list `[[x1,y1,x2,y2],…]`, each segment thickened to a band of the row's Width, or of a FIFTH column's width per segment. Polygon and Circle can only fill a CLOSED ring, so a centreline had to be widened into a quad by hand first.
A tilted segment needs no special case anywhere: the perpendicular frame is derived from the segment itself, so the vertical seat tube and the raked fork take the same path. Internally both 3D kinds emit a face list on the existing Polyhedron path, so the viewport, the 3D export and any downstream Display 3D handle them with no new shape.

AND ONE MATH-ENGINE CHANGE: hcat / vcat are now VARIADIC. Every row above is a nine-column record — `hcat(u1, v1, z1, u2, v2, z2, a, b, g)` — and this flow assembles 25 of them plus two spoke blocks, then joins the lot with a single `vcat`. Written pairwise that is five levels of nesting per row and twenty-six for the join, with the operands reading backwards; see `_Btop` in the table flow for what it looks like. Two operands behave exactly as before, the empty-operand identity that makes a loop accumulator work included.

ONE LIST, SIX GROUPS. Every part is authored in the bike's own frame (u along its length, v across, z up) as that nine-column record, where `a` and `b` carry whichever two numbers the part's row kind wants and `g` names its group: 1 frame, 2 fittings, 3 spokes, 4 tyres, 5 rims, 6 tyre plan footprints. The whole list is then mapped to world ONCE — two dot products per endpoint against the host frame's axes — and split back out with `compress(_W, eq(_g, k))`, `sub(…, 0, 0, _nr, 7)` trimming the group column off for a Tube row and `…, 8` leaving the section radius on for a Ring row. Adding a part is one more line and one more `vcat` operand; nothing else in the body moves.

WHY THE PLAN IS DERIVED, NOT DRAWN AGAIN. The 2D rows are the SAME segments with z dropped and the width taken from the same `a` column, so plan and model cannot disagree. A vertical member projects to a zero-length segment and the Stroke row drops it rather than drawing a spike — which is the correct top view of a seat tube. What survives is what a bike actually shows from above: two tyre bands, the splayed stays, the top and down tubes, the handlebar across, the saddle. Group 6 exists because a tyre is the one part whose plan footprint is NOT its 3D axis: the axle projects to a 40 mm square, so the two contact bands are authored separately, 2R long.

HOST-AWARE FITTING, as in the table. The host arrives on `val-points` as one row (a node), two (a segment) or many (a space outline); the opening block turns it into a frame — a segment's own direction, or a space's LONGEST edge — and a bounding box in that frame. A bike is RIGID, so Fit is a single UNIFORM scale rather than the table's per-axis stretch: Max shrinks it to fit the host's long axis and never enlarges, Exact fills that axis in both directions, Off leaves every dimension as typed. Clamped to 0.15–5× so a degenerate host cannot produce a bike the size of a building. Anchor Direction places the result by any of the nine box points, and Flip side mirrors the frame across the host axis (which side the drivetrain is on).

ROTATION, 0–360°, turns the bike about its host. It is applied where the frame is DERIVED, not to the finished geometry: the host axis is rotated once and the tubes, fittings, spokes, tyres, rims and all three plan rows are expressed in that frame, so one `hcat` of a 2×2 rotation carries every one of them and none can be left behind. On a node — the usual case — the host projects to a point and the bike simply spins on the spot; on a segment or a space the angle is RELATIVE to the host's own direction, and the fit box is re-measured in the turned frame, so Fit and Anchor keep meaning what they meant.

AND IT IS VERIFIED AS A RIGID MOTION, which is the only thing worth checking about one. Over 0 / 30 / 45 / 90 / 135 / 180 / 270 / 359 / 360° on a node host the farthest vertex from the node holds at 0.86520 m — a spread of 1.1e-13, floating-point noise — the solid keeps its z range of 0 → 1.038 m, and the ring and mesh counts never leave 21 and 5. The plan bounding box turns as it must: 1.72 × 0.44 at 0° and 180°, swapped at 90° and 270°, and 1.26 square on both diagonals. 0° and 360° agree to 0.000e+0, and mapping the 0° geometry through (x, y) → (−y, x) reproduces the 90° geometry to 0.000e+0 — so it is that exact rotation, not merely some displacement. Every metric — length, width, height, wheel diameter, saddle height, fit scale, footprint — is unchanged at 0°, 90° and 217°, as a rigid motion requires.

DIMENSIONS AT THE DEFAULTS: 1.73 m long, 0.44 m wide, 1.02 m tall, on 0.68 m wheels at a 1.05 m wheelbase with a 0.95 m saddle — a road bike within a centimetre or two of a real one. Fit = Max in a 1.2 m space scales it to 0.70×; in a 3 m space it stays 1.00× (Max never enlarges) while Exact takes it to 1.74×.

WHAT THIS STILL CANNOT DO. The frame is a fixed diamond — the tube TOPOLOGY is authored, not parametric, so a step-through or a full-suspension frame is a different body, not a different slider. Nothing is mitred: tubes interpenetrate at the joints rather than meeting cleanly, which reads correctly at these radii but is not a weldment. The wheels are upright and the bars are square to the frame, so there is no lean and no steering angle.

props.value: stylish, modern, lightweight road bike, glossy red frame, urban

params.name: Bike maths
params.expr:
_e1 = hcat(1, 0)
_n = rows(P)
_isSeg = _n == 2
_isSpace = _n > 2
_edges = _isSpace ? (shift(P, -1) - P) : _e1
_edgeLen = len(_edges)
_longest = max(_edgeLen)
_spaceDir = _isSpace ? row(compress(_edges, eq(_edgeLen, _longest)), 0) : _e1
_segDir = _isSeg ? (row(P, 1) - row(P, 0)) : _e1
_dir = _isSpace ? _spaceDir : (_isSeg ? _segDir : _e1)
_dirLen = len(_dir)
_axisB = _dirLen > 0 ? normalize(_dir) : _e1
_rot = rotation * PI / 180
_crot = cos(_rot)
_srot = sin(_rot)
_bx = sub(_axisB, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_by = sub(_axisB, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_axisU = hcat(_bx * _crot - _by * _srot, _bx * _srot + _by * _crot)
_axisV = (flipSide > 0 ? -1 : 1) * perp(_axisU)
_ux = sub(_axisU, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_uy = sub(_axisU, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_vx = sub(_axisV, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_vy = sub(_axisV, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_Qu = col(P, 0) * _ux + col(P, 1) * _uy
_Qv = col(P, 0) * _vx + col(P, 1) * _vy
_hu0 = _n > 0 ? min(_Qu) : 0
_hu1 = _n > 0 ? max(_Qu) : 0
_hv0 = _n > 0 ? min(_Qv) : 0
_hv1 = _n > 0 ? max(_Qv) : 0
_hcu = (_hu0 + _hu1) / 2
_hcv = (_hv0 + _hv1) / 2
_hostL = _hu1 - _hu0
_hostW = _hv1 - _hv0
_availL = max(0, _hostL - 2 * margin)
_natL = wheelbase + 2 * wheelR
_notOff = fitMode != 'Off'
_exact = fitMode == 'Exact'
_sRaw = _natL > 0 ? _availL / _natL : 1
_sFit = (_notOff && _availL > 0) ? (_exact ? _sRaw : min(1, _sRaw)) : 1
scale = max(0.15, min(5, _sFit))
_s = scale
_R = wheelR * _s
_TW = tyreW * _s
_WB = wheelbase * _s
_FR = frameR * _s
_BBH = bbHeight * _s
_SH = max(saddleHeight * _s, _BBH + 0.3 * _s)
_BH = max(barHeight * _s, _R + 0.35 * _s)
_BW = barWidth * _s
_bodyL = _WB + 2 * _R
_bodyW = max(_BW, 2.4 * _TW)
_anchorL = anchorDir == 'Top-Left' || anchorDir == 'Left-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Left'
_anchorR = anchorDir == 'Top-Right' || anchorDir == 'Right-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Right'
_anchorT = anchorDir == 'Top-Left' || anchorDir == 'Top-Center' || anchorDir == 'Top-Right'
_anchorB = anchorDir == 'Bottom-Left' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Right'
_ax = _anchorR - _anchorL
_ay = _anchorB - _anchorT
_hau = _hcu + _ax * max(0, _hostL / 2 - margin)
_hav = _hcv + _ay * max(0, _hostW / 2 - margin)
_cu = _hau - _ax * _bodyL / 2
_cv = _hav - _ay * _bodyW / 2
_ur = 0 - _WB / 2
_uf = _WB / 2
_ub = _ur + 0.4 * _WB
_us = _ub - 0.055 * _WB
_uh = _uf - 0.14 * _WB
_uk = _uf - 0.05 * _WB
_zk = min(_R + 0.26 * _s, _BH - 0.1 * _s)
_sv = 1.2 * _TW
_hubR = 0.035 * _s
_rimR = _R - 0.85 * _TW
_barR = 0.016 * _s
_sadR = 0.06 * _s
_crkR = 0.012 * _s
_axlR = 0.01 * _s
_spkR = 0.0045 * _s
_f1 = hcat(_ub, 0, _BBH, _us, 0, _SH, _FR, 0, 1)
_f2 = hcat(_us, 0, _SH, _uh, 0, _BH, _FR, 0, 1)
_f3 = hcat(_uk, 0, _zk, _uh, 0, _BH, _FR, 0, 1)
_f4 = hcat(_ub, 0, _BBH, _uk, 0, _zk, _FR, 0, 1)
_f5 = hcat(_ur, 0 - _sv, _R, _ub, 0, _BBH, _FR, 0, 1)
_f6 = hcat(_ur, _sv, _R, _ub, 0, _BBH, _FR, 0, 1)
_f7 = hcat(_ur, 0 - _sv, _R, _us, 0, _SH, _FR, 0, 1)
_f8 = hcat(_ur, _sv, _R, _us, 0, _SH, _FR, 0, 1)
_f9 = hcat(_uf, 0 - _sv, _R, _uk, 0, _zk, _FR, 0, 1)
_f10 = hcat(_uf, _sv, _R, _uk, 0, _zk, _FR, 0, 1)
_t1 = hcat(_uh, 0 - _BW / 2, _BH, _uh, _BW / 2, _BH, _barR, 0, 2)
_t2 = hcat(_us - 0.11 * _s, 0, _SH, _us + 0.1 * _s, 0, _SH, _sadR, 0, 2)
_t3 = hcat(_ub, 0 - 0.075 * _s, _BBH, _ub, 0.075 * _s, _BBH, _axlR, 0, 2)
_t4 = hcat(_ub, 0 - 0.075 * _s, _BBH, _ub - 0.165 * _s, 0 - 0.075 * _s, _BBH, _crkR, 0, 2)
_t5 = hcat(_ub, 0.075 * _s, _BBH, _ub + 0.165 * _s, 0.075 * _s, _BBH, _crkR, 0, 2)
_t6 = hcat(_ub - 0.165 * _s, 0 - 0.115 * _s, _BBH, _ub - 0.165 * _s, 0 - 0.035 * _s, _BBH, _crkR, 0, 2)
_t7 = hcat(_ub + 0.165 * _s, 0.035 * _s, _BBH, _ub + 0.165 * _s, 0.115 * _s, _BBH, _crkR, 0, 2)
_t8 = hcat(_ur, 0 - _sv, _R, _ur, _sv, _R, _axlR, 0, 2)
_t9 = hcat(_uf, 0 - _sv, _R, _uf, _sv, _R, _axlR, 0, 2)
_y1 = hcat(_ur, 0 - _TW / 2, _R, _ur, _TW / 2, _R, _R - _TW / 2, _TW / 2, 4)
_y2 = hcat(_uf, 0 - _TW / 2, _R, _uf, _TW / 2, _R, _R - _TW / 2, _TW / 2, 4)
_m1 = hcat(_ur, 0 - _TW / 3, _R, _ur, _TW / 3, _R, _rimR, 0.01 * _s, 5)
_m2 = hcat(_uf, 0 - _TW / 3, _R, _uf, _TW / 3, _R, _rimR, 0.01 * _s, 5)
_p1 = hcat(_ur - _R, 0, _R, _ur + _R, 0, _R, _TW / 2, 0, 6)
_p2 = hcat(_uf - _R, 0, _R, _uf + _R, 0, _R, _TW / 2, 0, 6)
_ns = max(3, floor(spokes))
_ang = arange(_ns) * 2 * PI / _ns
_cs = cos(_ang)
_sn = sin(_ang)
_z0 = zeros(_ns, 1)
_sr = fill(_ns, 1, _spkR)
_g3 = fill(_ns, 1, 3)
_sp1 = hcat(_ur + _hubR * _cs, _z0, _R + _hubR * _sn, _ur + _rimR * _cs, _z0, _R + _rimR * _sn, _sr, _z0, _g3)
_sp2 = hcat(_uf + _hubR * _cs, _z0, _R + _hubR * _sn, _uf + _rimR * _cs, _z0, _R + _rimR * _sn, _sr, _z0, _g3)
_LOC = vcat(_f1, _f2, _f3, _f4, _f5, _f6, _f7, _f8, _f9, _f10, _t1, _t2, _t3, _t4, _t5, _t6, _t7, _t8, _t9, _y1, _y2, _m1, _m2, _p1, _p2, _sp1, _sp2)
_U1 = _cu + col(_LOC, 0)
_V1 = _cv + col(_LOC, 1)
_U2 = _cu + col(_LOC, 3)
_V2 = _cv + col(_LOC, 4)
_W = hcat(_U1 * _ux + _V1 * _vx, _U1 * _uy + _V1 * _vy, col(_LOC, 2), _U2 * _ux + _V2 * _vx, _U2 * _uy + _V2 * _vy, col(_LOC, 5), col(_LOC, 6), col(_LOC, 7), col(_LOC, 8))
_g = col(_W, 8)
_nr = rows(_W)
_frame = compress(_W, eq(_g, 1))
_fit = compress(_W, eq(_g, 2))
_spoke = compress(_W, eq(_g, 3))
_tyre = compress(_W, eq(_g, 4))
_rim = compress(_W, eq(_g, 5))
_plan = compress(_W, eq(_g, 6))
Frame3D = sub(_frame, 0, 0, _nr, 7)
Fittings3D = sub(_fit, 0, 0, _nr, 7)
Spokes3D = sub(_spoke, 0, 0, _nr, 7)
Tyres3D = sub(_tyre, 0, 0, _nr, 8)
Rims3D = sub(_rim, 0, 0, _nr, 8)
FramePlan = hcat(col(_frame, 0), col(_frame, 1), col(_frame, 3), col(_frame, 4), 2 * col(_frame, 6))
FittingsPlan = hcat(col(_fit, 0), col(_fit, 1), col(_fit, 3), col(_fit, 4), 2 * col(_fit, 6))
TyresPlan = hcat(col(_plan, 0), col(_plan, 1), col(_plan, 3), col(_plan, 4), 2 * col(_plan, 6))
length = _bodyL
width = _bodyW
height = max(_BH, _SH)
wheelDia = 2 * _R
saddleHeight = _SH
footprint = _bodyL * _bodyW
